vs

full_judgment:
a. Begum Sufia Akhter, wife of Mvi Ali Ahmed Majumder by way of a deed of conveyance dated 16-3-1957 from Nirupoma Dey and others became owner and possessor of suit property. During State Acquisition Survey operation suit property along with another property stood recorded in the name of Sufia Akhter. Sufia Akhter constructed two separate buildings with good number of rooms and rented rooms on monthly basis to different persons and through monthly tenants remained owner of tenanted shop rooms/premises. 

 c. Two sons of Sufia Akhter Abu Md Shah Newaz and Abu Md Rahe Newaz being owners and possessors of suit property and building standing thereon along with another item of property executed and registered a deed of exchange or ewaz themselves on 29-6-1997. In accordance with recital in the deed of exchange Abu Md Shah Newaz got suit property and building named Khaza Mansion standing on suit property and his other brother Abu Md Rahe Newaz got other property and building named Sufia Mansion standing thereon and both of them in the exercise of their right, interest and possession were in exclusive possession of exchanged properties and buildings standing thereon. Abu Md Shah Newaz inducted different persons on suit property and building named Khaja Mansion as monthly tenants and remained owner of property. Abu Md Shah Newaz subsequently constructed another building and rented the same on monthly basis to different persons, Schedule property and building standing thereon stood recorded correctly in the name of Abu Md Shah Newaz in present Khatian No. 578. 

 d. Abu Md Shah Newaz having being owner and possessor of Khaja Mansion buildings transferred the same by way of a duly executed and registered sale deed dated 26-11-2000 in favour of plaintiffs and plaintiffs since purchase remained absolute owners of said purchased property on mutating their names and separating jamas and recording their names in concerned khatian and on paying rents regularly and opening a holding in their names with Pourashava. 

 e. Sole-defendant took rent in respect of suit property and shop room on a monthly rent of Taka 2,000 from vendor of plaintiffs with condition of payment of monthly rent within 7th day of following month and sole-defendant was only a temporary monthly tenant. defendant having been a tenant, plaintiffs before their purchase had conversation with him. Plaintiffs since their purchase asked defendant-opposite party to satisfy monthly rent in respect of schedule shop, and, also; to receive receipts as evidences of payments of rent but defendant-opposite party did not pay any heed to the request offered by plaintiff towards him. Plaintiffs on 17-3-2001 issued an Attornment Notice upon defendant and made a request to him to realise arrear rent and current rent in respect of rented shop. Attorney Notice had been duly served upon defendant on 20-3-2001. In spite of receipt of Attorney Notice defendant did not pay any rent to plaintiffs. Defendant, thus, became a habitual defaulter, plaintiff, thereafter, issued a registered notice on 7-5-2001 under section 106 of The Transfer of Property Act. The notice having not been received by defendant stood returned back. On 14-5-2001 defendant in spite of notice did not hand over vacant possession of schedule shop room in favour of plaintiffs. Plaintiffs, thus, had been constrained to institute suit in Small Causes Court. 

 e. Two sons of Sufia Akhter, Abu Md Shah Newaz and Abu Md Rahe Newaz became owners of property from their mother Sufia Akhter on the strength of registered deed of gift dated 27-4-1991. Abu Md Rahe Newaz got suit property in view of amicable settlement entered into by two brothers and Abu Md Rahe Newaz by way of that amicable settlement got suit property and became absolute owners and Abu Md Shah Newaz did not get suit property and premises and a Baratia agreement has been executed on 31-12-1996 in between defendant Md Jalaluddin and Md Rokonuddin Chowdhury as second party and Abu Md Rahe Newaz being first party and on the basis of Baratia agreement Abu Md Rahe Newaz rented 1-7 rooms of suit premises in favour of Md Jalaluddin and Md Rokanuddin Chowdhury. 

 g. A decision had been reached between Abu Md Rahe Newaz and defendant that latter would offer Taka 5,50,000 to Abu Md Rahe Newaz and on certain conditions a fresh Baratia agreement had been executed on 15-4-1997 in between defendant and Abu Md Rahe Newaz and defendant in that way became tenant in respect of 8 shops under Baratia agreement dated 15-4-1997. Defendant subsequently became aware in respect of a deed of exchange dated 29-6-1997 between two brothers, Abu Md Shah Newaz and Abu Md Rahe Newaz. defendant, also, became aware that Dr Abu Md Shah Newaz got schedule Baratia premises in his saham. Abu Md Shah Newaz entered into an agreement for sale in regard to schedule premises and shops and other buildings with Md Anwarul Hoque on a consideration of Taka 8,00,000 and an agreement had been executed on 29-6-1997 on receipt of Taka 6,00,000 by Abu Md Shah Newaz and Abu Md Shah Newaz handed over possession of part property under agreement. Defendant, thereafter, admitted Md Anwarul Hoque as landlord owner and promised to pay rent regularly through rent receipts. Anwarul Hoque admitted defendant as his tenant and accepted rents from him. 

 h. Defendant recently came to know that Abu Md Shah Newaz did not accept balance consideration money from Anwarul Hoque and did not execute and register sale deed in favour of Anwarul Hoque and transferred schedule property in favour of plaintiffs by a registered deed. Plaintiffs having been aware of agreement for sale deed dated 29-6-1997 created deed of conveyance in respect of suit property and premises. Anwarul Hoque, thereafter, instituted a suit being Title Suit No.24 of 2001 in First Court of Subordinate Judge, Comilla impleading Abu Md Shah Newaz as First defendant and present plaintiffs as Second-Fourth defendants. Defendant since 1-1-1998 had been paying rents to Anwarul Hoque. In the event of decision arrived at in Title Suit No. 24 of 2001 in respect of ownership of suit shop and premises, defendant could pay rents to plaintiffs, otherwise not. 

 i. Defendant Jubair Alam Sarker by way of agreement had been satisfying rents regularly and he could not be treated as defaulter for non-payment of rent. 

 iii. Payment of rent by defendant with Rent Controller had been established. 

 i. Whether defendant-opposite party is liable to be evicted from the suit/shop premises on the ground of default of payment of rent to plaintiffs-petitioners 

 Exhibits 5 and 6 are corrected Records of Right and separated Khatian Nos. 862/578 prepared in name of Abu Md Shah Newaz in respect of exchanged property which, also, included suit shop/premises. Exhibit 7 is Deed of Conveyance dated 26-11-2000 executed and registered in favour of plaintiffs by Abu Md Shah Newaz and Schedule property in deed of conveyance is exchanged property/suit property i.e. suit shop and premises. Exhibit 8 is corrected Record of Right i.e. Khatian No. 1003 prepared in the name of plaintiff-petitioners and property covered in Record of Right is suit property/suit shop/premises. Exhibit 8(ka) is Duplicate Car-bon Receipt in respect of Sub-Division of Holding Case No. 526 of 2000-2001 in the name of plaintiffs. Exhibit 9 is rent Receipt evidencing payment of rent of Government in respect of suit shop/premises. Exhibit 10 (ka) are Comilla Pourashava Receipts in regard to suit shop/ premises holding for years 2002-2004 AD holding No being 81 / 77(Ka). Exhibit 11 is Attornment Notice dated 17-3-2001 issued by plaintiffs in favour of defendant-opposite party. Exhibit 12 is Notice dated 7-5-2001 under section 106 of Transfer of Property Act asking defendant opposite party to hand over vacant possession of suit shop/premises in favour of Notice Giver-plaintiff. Exhibit Ka series are House Rent Receipts in name of Anwarul Huq by defendant-opposite party from 8-2-1998 -10-2-2001. Exhibit Ga is the order of dismissal of Title Suit No. 24 of 2001 dated 25-10-2003 on strength of Solenama (Compromise), Md Anwarul Huq being plaintiff and Abu Md Shah Newaz and Amena Begum, Md Zakir Hussain Chowdhury and Md Zahedul Hussain Chowdhury (plaintiffs) being defendants. The suit was for a decree of Specific Performance of Contract in respect of suit shop/premises against defendants of suit. Exhibit Ga(1) is sole decree recorded in Title Suit No. 24 of 2001. Exhibit Ga(2) is Petition of Compromise entered into between plaintiff and First-Fourth defendants of suit. Annexure A to Civil Revision Petition is a petition dated 10-2-2004 presented before Rent Controller and Sadar Senior Assistant Judge, Comilla by defendant-opposite party in Case No. 28 of 2002 under section 19 of Rent Control Ordinance seeking permission to deposit rent in the name of First Third opposite parties who are plaintiff in Small Causes Court Suit in place of Fourth opposite party who is Md Anwarul Huq from the present month i.e. from the month of February, 2004. Annexure Al is the order passed by Rent Controller and Sadar Senior Assistant Judge, Comilla according permission to applicant of the Miscellaneous Case Md Zubair Alam Sarkar (defendant-opposite party). Annexure B and B1 are chalans evidencing deposit of Rents in the name of opposite parties in Miscellaneous Case who are plaintiffs-petitioners in Civil Revision Case. 

 18. Exhibit 4, Deed of Exchange dated 29-6-1997 demonstrates that Abu Md Shah Newaz became the owner of the suit shop/premises. Exhibit 7, deed of conveyance dated 26-11-2000 is evidence that Abu Md Shah Newaz transferred all the right, title and interest of suit shop/premises in favour of plaintiffs-petitioners and plaintiffs-petitioners became absolute owners of suit shop/premises and plaintiffs-petitioners stopped into the shoes of Abu Md Shah Newaz. Exhibit 8, Record of Right prepared in the name of plaintiffs-petitioners, Exhibit 8 (ka), 9, 10, 10(ka) are all evidences of acquisition of right, title, interest of the plaintiffs-petitioners over suit shop/premises.  It is posited that ownership is de jure recognition of a claim to a property. Ownership is pre-eminently a right. The right to ownership of a property carries with it the right to its enjoyment and other beneficial enjoyments  incidental thereto. Possession is de facto exercise of the right to property. Attornment Notice dated 17-3-2001, Exhibit 11 indicates that on 17-3-2001 plaintiffs-petitioners as Notice Givers issued Notice upon defendant-opposite party asking him to satisfy arrear rents and present month rent to them. The word "attorn" means transfer; make legal acknowledgment of the new Landlord. Attornment by tenant means acceptance of new owner as Landlord and estopping the tenant to dispute Landlord's title thereto. Relevant portion of Attornment Notice is extracted hereunder: 

 Defendnat-opposite party in spite of Attornment Notice did not admit new owners, plaintiffs-petitioners as landlords and, in spite of Notice under section 106 of Transfer of Property Act did not pay rent to plaintiffs-petitioners and, thus, became habitual defaulter making him liable to be evicted from suit shop/ premises. 

 Further averment made by defendant-opposite party in written statement is that he admitted Anwarul Huq as owner of suit premises and Anwarul Huq admitted defendant-opposite party as tenant and received rent from him and defendant had been paying rent to Anwarul Huq since 1-1-1998. Relevant portion of statement is in following language: 

 Defendant-opposite party accepted Anwarul Huq as owner of suit shop/premises on the strength of an agreement for sale. But mere agreement for sale did not confer any title on Anwarul Huq Section 54 of Transfer of Property Act can be pressed into service in this regard which enjoins that a contract for sale of immovable property is a contract that a sale of such property shall take place on terms settled between parties and it does not, of itself, create any interest in or charge on such property. Anwarul Huq could not become owner of suit shop/premises on the strength of alleged agreement for sale entered between him and Abu Md Shah Newaz and there could not be any legal justification to pay rent to Anwarul Huq and payment of rent to Anwarul Huq by defendant-opposite party as owner of suit shop /premises is no payment of rent in eye of law. 

 20. It is lip evidence of defendant-opposite party as DW 1 that western portion of property (suit property) fell in saham of Lablu (Abu Md Shah Newaz) and out of two brothers Abu Md Shah Newaz Lablu got suit Market by way of amicable settlement and Abu Md Shah Newaz got possession over entire market and Shah Newaz, realised rent from other tenants except him and that he was well aware of deed of partition (Deed of Exchange) and he was a witness to deed of partition (Exchange Deed). Relevant portions of version provided by defendant-opposite party No. 1 as DW 1 are extracted below: 

 21. From statements made in written statement dated 18-4-2002 and testimony furnished by defendant-opposite party point had been crystallised that defendant-opposite party became aware in respect of Iwaz deed dated 29-6-1997 between two brothers, Abu Md Shah Newaz and Abu Md Rahe Newaz and that Abu Md Shah Newaz got schedule (suit) shop/premises by way of deed of exchange. Defendant-opposite party in spite of clear knowledge of deed of exchange, and, also, of getting of suit shop/premises in saham of Abu Md Shah Newaz and, also, of the deed of conveyance executed and registered on 26-11-2000 by Abu Md Shah Newaz in favour of plaintiffs-petitioners and, also, in spite of receipt of Attornment Notice, Exhibit 11 and Notice under section 106 of Transfer of Property Act did neither attorn nor admit plaintiffs-petitioners as owner and landlord of suit shop-premises and did not pay rent to them and, thus, became habitual defaulter rendering him liable to be evicted from suit shop/premises. 

 Defendant-opposite party having admitted himself as tenant under Anwarul Huq was very much bound by the sole-decree recorded in Title Suit No. 24 of 2001. Defendant-opposite parties even in the face of dismissal of suit filed by his alleged Landlord Anwarul Huq by way of solenama following sole-decree did not care to admit plaintiffs-petitioners as owners/land-lords on suit shop/premises and did not care to pay rent from being saved to be adjudged as defaulters. 

 23. Annexure A to Civil Revision Petition is a petition dated 10-2-2004 submitted in Miscellaneous Rent Case No. 28 of 2002 by defendant-opposite party seeking permission to Rent Controller for depositing rent in the name of plaintiffs-petitioners in place of Anwarul Huq. But defendant opposite party became a defaulter long before bestowing the petition before Rent Controller and Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Comilla for depositing rent in the name of plaintiffs-petitioners. This petition laid by defendant-petitioner for depositing rent before rent before rent Controller and according permission to defendant-opposite-party for depositing rent and deposit of rent by Challans, Annexures B, B1 and B2 could not and cannot save defendant opposite-party from being a defaulter/defendant is default, whether habitual or not. defendant-opposite party could deposit rent with Rent Controller immediately after dismissal of Title Suit laid by Anwarul Huq for Specific Performance of Contract and it was too late in the day to deposit rent with Rent Controller and defendant-opposite party could not save himself from being a defaulter. 

 24. Payment of rents to Anwarul Huq is no legal payment of rent in asmuchas Anwarul Huq could not be owner/landlord of the suit shop/premises on the strength of an Agreement for sale in asmuchas an Agreement for sale did not confer any title and ownership upon Anwarul Huq. Small Cause Court fell into a serious error in holding that defendant Zobair Alam Sarker by way of agreement had been paying rents regularly and he could not be treated as defaulter for non-payment of rent and by this error the merit of decision of the case has been seriously affected. 

 25. From the above discussion, the irresistible conclusion which can be drawn is that defendant opposite party has established himself as a defaulter in payment of rent to owner/ landlord who are no other than plaintiffs-petitioners and plaintiffs-petitioners could prove through legal evidence that defendant-opposite party is a defaulter. Result that follows is that defendant opposite party is to be evicted from suit shop/premises. 

 26. Small Cause Court Judge misdirected himself in total approach of the legal debate involved in the suit. Plaintiffs-petitioners as transferees/purchasers of suit shop /premises from the rightful owner-transferor Abu Md Shah Newaz were and are entitled to rent from the date of transfer of ownership in the property and relationship of landlord and tenant had been established between plaintiffs-petitioners and defendant opposite party from the date of transfer of ownership of suit shop/ premises. Plaintiffs-petitioners served Attornment Notice upon defendant-opposite party and the said Notice had been received by the latter as evidenced from acknowledgment receipt. But defendant-opposite party did not care to pay rent to plaintiffs-petitioners in compliance with Attornment Notice. Finding reached by Small Causes Court Judge to the effect that relationship of landlord and tenant had not been established between plaintiffs and defendant suffers from gross illegality and legal infirmity. 

 27. Small Causes Court Judge, also, committed a substantial error in rendering decision that payment of rent by defendant with Rent Controller had been established inasmuch as plaintiffs-petitioners became entitled to rent from defendant-opposite party from the date of acquisition of ownership on suit shop/premises on the baluster of deed of transfer from owner-vendor Abu Md Shah Newaz and, thereafter, on service of Attornment Notice upon defendant-opposite party and defendant-opposite party became defaulter long before his laying of petition before Rent Controller for according permission to deposit rent with it and by deposit of rent (Annexure A, B and B1 respectively) to Rent Controller defendant-petitioner could not and cannot at all derive any benefit of provision engrafted in section 19 of Premises Rent Control Act of 1991. Payment of rent by defendant-petitioner only on 6-3-2006 and 6-4-2006 with Rent Controller is no lawful payment of rent and defendant-opposite party cannot save himself from being evicted from suit shop/premises and he has rendered himself liable to be evicted from suit shop/ premises. 

 28. Small Causes Court Judge, also, has been in grave error in holding that dispute having been cropped up in respect of title between parties, the suit as framed is not maintainable. No dispute arose in respect of title over suit shop/premises. Ownership and title over suit shop /premises on the part of plaintiffs-petitioners is undisputed and invincible and defendant-opposite party, also, admitted absolute ownership of plaintiffs-petitioners and, also, took plaintiffs-petitioners as landords by petition laid before Rent Controller Annexure 'A' to Civil Revision Petition. Finding reached by Small Cause Court Judge on this point perilously borders on perversity.
